abstract: Co-transcriptional chromatin regulation is widely recognized as a mechanism that reinforces active gene expression, yet transcriptionally active genes must also be able to transition into stable epigenetic silencing during developmental transitions and environmental responses. Whether and how ongoing transcription is coupled to the initiation of epigenetic silencing remains unclear. Here we show that elongating RNA polymerase II phosphorylated at Ser2 (RNAPII-Ser2P) functions as an instructive signal for epigenetic silencing initiation. At actively transcribed genes, RNAPII-Ser2P positions and spatially constrains the FLD-LD H3K4me1 demethylase complex near transcription termination regions, separating the complex from its gene-body H3K4me1 substrate. We found that both chemical perturbation of transcription and physiological silencing cues induce a redistribution of RNAPII-Ser2P into the gene body, accompanied by FLD relocalization and subsequent gene-body H3K4me1 erasure. FLD disengages from chromatin upon gene silencing, indicating that active transcription is required for its continued chromatin association. We further show that LD tethers FLD to RNAPII through an N-terminal HOX domain that binds the C-terminal region of FLD and an adjacent TFIIS domain that contacts the RNAPII CTD in a Ser2P-sensitive manner. This FLD-LD-RNAPII bridge is essential to promote H3K4me1 erasure and gene silencing. Together, these findings reveal a mechanism by which active transcription licenses the initiation of epigenetic silencing.
